## Description

This document shows the process for tidying the scraped data from the San Diego County Traffic Advisory Committee's 2019 Traffic Study including Sandia Creek Road. Sandia Creek Road is a striped two-lane local roadway 25-feet in width. The roadway is striped with a no passing centerline. There are speed advisory curves along the segment. The roadway is classified as a Minor Collector (2.3C) in the County General Plan Mobility Element Network primarily intended for residential neighborhoods or for rural areas with steep slopes and physical constraints. The roadway has a 55 MPH unposted speed zone.

The raw data was extracted from the tables within a PDF.

## Load Packages

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(here)
```

# Part 1: 2019 2-day Traffic Study

## Load Data

```{r}
traffic_data_2019_orig <- read_csv(here("traffic_study_data", "traffic_volume_2019-08_combined.csv"))
```

## Make data "tidy"

```{r}
traffic_data_2019 <- traffic_data_2019_orig |>
  clean_names() |>
  select(date:wb) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = nb:wb,
               names_to = "direction",
               values_to = "count")
```

# Part 2: 2024 1-day Traffic Study

## Load Data

```{r}
traffic_data_2024_orig <- read_csv(here("data", "volume_2024-10-15.csv"))
```

## Make data "tidy"

```{r}
traffic_data_2024 <- traffic_data_2024_orig |>
  clean_names() |>
  select(date, day, time, nb, sb, eb, wb)|>
  pivot_longer(cols = nb:wb,
               names_to = "direction",
               values_to = "count")
```

## Combine all traffic data (72 hours total)

```{r}
traffic_data <- bind_rows(traffic_data_2019, traffic_data_2024)
```

## Save as CSV

```{r}
write_csv(traffic_data, here("data", "traffic_data.csv"))
```
